scenes.title: Mass times velocity

beats.text: For a moving trolley, momentum equals mass times velocity.
In symbols, p equals m v. The mass is m, and the velocity is v.
Multiply kilograms by metres per second. That gives momentum in kilogram metres per second.
Velocity includes direction, so momentum does too. Mass is positive, so momentum's arrow points the same way as velocity.
beats.caption: Momentum has magnitude and direction.

scenes.title: Two trolleys on separate tracks

beats.text: Consider two trolleys on separate parallel tracks. Trolley A travels to the right, while trolley B travels to the left.
Watch their motion. A is moving faster. The separate tracks mean they pass without colliding.
Now freeze this picture so we can label the whole question.
beats.caption: Snapshot for calculation.

scenes.title: The whole question

beats.text: Trolley A has mass two kilograms and moves right at six metres per second.
Trolley B has mass three kilograms and moves left at four metres per second.
The tracks are separate. Take right as positive.
Find each signed momentum, then compare their magnitudes and directions. All the information is here before we calculate.

scenes.text: Trolley A has mass two kilograms and moves right at six metres per second. Trolley B has mass three kilograms and moves left at four metres per second. The tracks are separate. Take right as positive. Find each signed momentum, then compare their magnitudes and directions. All the information is here before we calculate.

scenes.title: Trolley A: choose the sign first

beats.text: Let's find trolley A's momentum. Why choose a direction before doing the arithmetic? Right is positive, and A moves right.
Start with the rule in words: momentum equals mass times velocity.
In symbols, p equals m v. It is velocity that carries the sign.
The speed is six metres per second. Because right is positive, the velocity is plus six metres per second.
The mass is two kilograms. Substitute two times plus six into the formula.
That gives plus twelve kilogram metres per second.
The positive sign means rightwards. Keep that direction with the answer; the number alone does not give the whole vector.
beats.caption: Positive momentum points right.

scenes.title: Trolley B: a negative momentum

beats.text: Now consider trolley B. Keep right positive. This trolley moves left, so its velocity must carry a minus sign. Its mass stays positive.
Again, momentum equals mass times velocity.
Write p equals m v before putting in the numbers.
Its speed is four metres per second. Because left is negative, write the velocity as minus four metres per second.
Use the mass, three kilograms: three times minus four.
The momentum is minus twelve kilogram metres per second.
The minus sign tells us left, not a negative mass.
Compare both results. Their magnitudes are equal, but their momentum arrows point in opposite directions. Equal magnitude alone does not mean equal momentum.
beats.caption: Equal magnitudes; opposite directions.

scenes.title: What if left becomes positive?

beats.text: Keep the same masses and actual motion. What would change if we chose left as positive? Find both signed momenta. Does either trolley turn around?
Only our sign convention changes. Momentum still equals mass times velocity.
Write p equals m v.
A still moves right, now negative. Use two times minus six.
A's momentum is minus twelve kilogram metres per second.
B still moves left, now positive. Use three times plus four.
B's momentum is plus twelve kilogram metres per second.
Neither trolley turns around. Changing which direction we call positive changes the signs, while the physical directions stay the same.
beats.caption: New signs; unchanged physical directions.
